claims.claim: In the ordinary Torus Puzzle, where either direction of every unit push is available, SwapPairs applies an involution with k transpositions to a specified b-cell row in exactly 3b+3k pushes, shifts the off-row bodies of the same k auxiliary columns by one chosen step, and fixes every other position; the transposed statement holds for columns.
claims.evidence: Each of the three SwapPairs phases makes exactly b row pushes and touches each of the k auxiliary columns once. In the bidirectional model, every source occurrence of a−1 forward column pushes is exactly one inverse unit push. Direct position tracking gives the stated row transpositions, one signed cyclic shift on each auxiliary off-row body, and identity elsewhere. Transposition gives the column form.
claims.witness: The literal three-phase word has length 3b+3k. Exhaustive checks covered 7,890 cases for 2≤a≤6 and 2≤b≤7, all partial matchings and both body-shift directions.
claims.search_method: Symbolic permutation tracking followed by exhaustive exact tuple-permutation simulation.

claims.claim: On an a×b board with a,b≥2, every even permutation of one specified row is realizable in at most 9b unit pushes while fixing every other position; every even permutation of one specified column is realizable in at most 9a. If a or b is even, every permutation of one specified row or column is realizable in O(a+b) pushes while fixing all other positions.
claims.evidence: An even line permutation factors into two involutions having the same transposition count k≤b/2. Oppositely directed SwapPairs calls cancel their identical auxiliary-body effects and cost 2(3b+3k)≤9b. For an odd permutation, an even-length line has an odd unit rotation, reducing to the even case. If the line is odd and the perpendicular dimension is even, a single-transposition SwapPairs leaves a cycle of odd body length, hence an even side-effect permutation whose inverse is handled by the even perpendicular-line construction. All constructions fix positions outside the requested line after cancellation.
claims.witness: All even permutations of lengths 2 through 7 were factorized and simulated on heights 2, 3, and 4, giving 8,868 checked realizations; 38 representative exhaustive odd-line realizations covered both parity branches and their transposes.
claims.search_method: Independent involution enumeration, parity analysis, and exact word simulation.

claims.claim: Two equal adjacent transpositions on rows r<s can be performed exactly in 8(s−r) pushes; the analogous claim holds for columns. A horizontal and a vertical adjacent transposition sharing one cell can be performed in four pushes.
claims.evidence: A row-column commutator or its inverse is an L-supported 3-cycle. On a 2×2 rectangle, the left-to-right identity (x y z)(x w z)=(x y)(z w) gives equal horizontal adjacent transpositions on two neighboring rows in eight pushes. Concatenating these gadgets along rows r,r+1,…,s cancels each intermediate transposition twice and has exactly 8(s−r) pushes. A horizontal and vertical transposition sharing a cell compose to either orientation of the same L-cycle.
claims.witness: Exact simulation checked 784 commutators, 140 neighboring parallel-transposition pairs, and 392 perpendicular-transposition products on every board with dimensions from 2 through 5.
claims.search_method: General support calculation plus exhaustive exact permutation identities on small dimensions.

claims.claim: A layer consisting of an independent permutation in every row, or in every column, can be performed in O(ab) pushes whenever its global permutation is even. If at least one board dimension is even, an arbitrary row layer or column layer can be performed in O(ab) pushes.
claims.evidence: Use one fixed adjacent transposition h to factor every odd constituent row permutation as an even permutation followed by h. The even constituents cost at most 9ab total. Global evenness makes the number of residual h's even; pairing affected rows consecutively costs 8 times a total gap at most a−1. If the layer is odd and a dimension is even, all but one residual are paired and the last is handled by Claim 1 in O(a+b)=O(ab). The column argument is the transpose.
claims.witness: For affected rows r1<…<r2q, the residual cost is 8Σj(r2j−r2j−1)≤8(a−1); the constituent even-line cost is at most 9ab.
claims.search_method: Parity decomposition, disjoint-support composition, and exact verification of the component gadgets.

claims.claim: Under the structured hypothesis of the audited parent—every non-buffer token is in its target row and all target-column-1 tokens occupy column 1—every sortable board can be completed in O(mn) pushes.
claims.evidence: The correction consists of a column-1 permutation β and a row layer Π that fixes column 1. Thus β and Π have disjoint support and commute. On an odd×odd board, sortability gives sign(β)=sign(Π). If both are odd, choose an odd row of Π, let H be an adjacent horizontal transposition there involving column 1, and let V be an adjacent vertical transposition in column 1 sharing that cell. With β=V E_C and Π=E_R H, commutation gives βΠ=Πβ=E_R(HV)E_C; E_R and E_C are even layers and HV is a four-push L-cycle. This also resolves the proof sketch's unstated ordering step.
claims.witness: All 24 even structured correction permutations on 3×3 were checked; 12 exercised the odd-odd branch and satisfied the commuted factorization exactly.
claims.search_method: Support analysis, parity factorization, and exhaustive exact structured-case simulation.

claims.claim: Every permutation P of the positions of an a×b board has a constructive row-column-row factorization P=A B C, where A and C independently permute positions inside rows and B independently permutes positions inside columns.
claims.evidence: The multigraph between source rows and target rows is b-regular. For every left set X, its b|X| incident edges enter neighbors having total capacity b|Γ(X)|, proving Hall's condition. Repeated perfect-matching removal therefore gives b colors. The first row layer sends each token to its color column, the column layer sends it to its target row, and the final row layer sends it to its target column. Tracking each token proves P=ABC under the source's left-to-right convention.
claims.witness: A constructive matching implementation reproduced ABC=P for all 720 permutations on both 2×3 and 3×2, and for all 181,440 even permutations on 3×3 used in the parity audit.
claims.search_method: Independent Hall proof and exact constructive edge-coloring simulation.

claims.claim: For a,b≥2, every position permutation is realizable in O(ab) unit pushes if a or b is even, while every even position permutation is realizable in O(ab) pushes if both dimensions are odd.
claims.evidence: Apply Claim 5 and realize its three layers using Claim 3. In the odd×odd case an even P has either zero or two odd factors. Adjacent odd factors are written E_A H and V E_B, with H and V sharing a cell, so their product is a four-push L-cycle. If only the two row layers are odd, let S swap the same two columns in every row. Because the number of rows is odd, S is odd, and (AS)(S⁻¹BS)(S⁻¹C)=ABC consists of row, column, row layers that are all even. These cases exhaust the parity patterns and all costs have absolute O(ab) constants.
claims.witness: Every one of the 181,440 even permutations on 3×3 passed constructive factorization and parity normalization: 46,332 all-even, 44,388 first-row/column odd, 46,332 column/final-row odd, and 44,388 separated-row odd cases.
claims.search_method: Complete parity-case proof plus exhaustive exact 3×3 normalization and complete 2×3/3×2 routing checks.

claims.claim: Every instance A has pn(A)≥ceil(H(A)/n)+ceil(V(A)/m). A global translation by a columns and b rows has exact push number m·d_n(a)+n·d_m(b), where d_k(z)=min(z mod k,k−(z mod k)).
claims.evidence: A row push changes each affected token's cyclic horizontal distance by at most one, so decreases H by at most n; column pushes leave H unchanged. The symmetric statement holds for V, and the required row and column push counts add. A translation has H=mn·d_n(a) and V=mn·d_m(b), giving the stated lower bound. Pushing every row and every column in shortest reverse directions attains it exactly.
claims.witness: The displacement lower bound was checked against exact BFS distances for all 24 states of 2×2 and all 720 states of 2×3.
claims.search_method: Per-generator Lipschitz proof and exhaustive comparison with exact small-board distances.

claims.claim: For all m,n≥1 with N=mn>1, the Torus Puzzle push-number diameter satisfies D(m,n)=Θ(N). More precisely, if m,n≥2 then 2N/3≤D(m,n)≤C N for an absolute constant C, while if min{m,n}=1 then D(m,n)=floor(N/2).
claims.evidence: Claim 6 supplies an absolute O(N) construction for every sortable permutation when both dimensions are nontrivial. Translating by floor(n/2) columns and floor(m/2) rows has exact distance m floor(n/2)+n floor(m/2)≥2N/3. In one dimension the reachable configurations are precisely the cyclic shifts of the sole nontrivial line, whose bidirectional cycle diameter is floor(N/2).
claims.witness: The lower-bound witness is the half-translation; Claim 6 supplies the matching uniform upper bound. Exact BFS additionally confirms the theorem on 2×2 and 2×3.
claims.search_method: Deductive combination of the constructive upper bound and exact translation certificate, with complete small-board BFS checks.

claims.claim: Let N=mn, s=min{m,n}, and t=max{m,n}. The audited upper bound D(m,n)=O(N·min{s,log t}) remains valid and is strictly strengthened to D(m,n)=O(N).
claims.evidence: Claim 8 proves the uniform O(N) bound. For every N>1, min{s,log t} is bounded below by a positive absolute constant, so O(N) implies the earlier bound. It is genuinely stronger over families where min{s,log t} is unbounded.
claims.witness: For square boards with side k, the former expression is O(k² log k) while the new bound is O(k²).
claims.search_method: Direct asymptotic implication from Claim 8; no computation needed.

claims.claim: For every fixed s≥2, boards with min{m,n}=s have asymptotically tight push number D(m,n)=Θ(mn).
claims.evidence: This follows immediately from the absolute bounds 2mn/3≤D(m,n)≤Cmn of Claim 8, which remain uniform when the smaller dimension is fixed.
claims.witness: For dimensions s×t with fixed s≥2, the half-translation has distance at least 2st/3 and the constructive algorithm uses at most Cst pushes.
claims.search_method: Direct specialization of the proved uniform theorem.

claims.claim: For m,n≥2, D(m,n)≥ceil(log_{d−1}(1+(d−2)(Q−1)/d)), where d=2(m+n), Q=(mn)! if m or n is even, and Q=(mn)!/2 otherwise.
claims.evidence: There are Q reachable configurations by the parity characterization. A geodesic cannot contain an adjacent generator-inverse pair. Hence at most 1+d((d−1)^L−1)/(d−2) nominal reduced words have length at most L. Duplicate direction labels on length-two lines only increase this count, so it remains a valid upper bound on the ball. Substituting L=D and rearranging gives the displayed ceiling exactly.
claims.witness: The checker evaluated the integer form on 2×2, 2×3, and 3×3, obtaining respective lower bounds 2, 3, and 5, consistent with exact diameters where enumerated.
claims.search_method: Independent reduced-word counting and exact integer evaluation on small boards.

claims.claim: Global translations are not generally diametral: D(2,3)=7, whereas every translated 2×3 board has distance at most 5.
claims.evidence: An independent BFS using the seven distinct 2×3 generators reached all 720 permutations with levels [1,7,31,115,274,253,36,3], so the diameter is 7. The six global translations have distances [0,2,2,3,5,5], with maximum 5.
claims.witness: The exact BFS level histogram sums to 720 and has a nonempty level 7; exhaustive translation lookup gives maximum distance 5.
claims.search_method: Complete exact breadth-first search over tuple permutations, without external data.

target_evidence: The draft supplies a complete matching pair of uniform bounds. Claims 0–3 establish O(ab) realizations of parity-compatible row and column layers; Claim 5 gives a constructive row-column-row factorization; Claim 6 resolves every parity pattern and yields an absolute O(mn) upper bound for every sortable nondegenerate board. Claim 7's half-translation gives at least 2mn/3 pushes, and the one-dimensional case is exact. Therefore D(m,n)=Θ(mn), closing the source's multiplicative logarithmic gap at the requested asymptotic strength. The structured proof's implicit commutation step was independently checked and does not invalidate the result.
